thread: Follow the swarm from the boards and counters of traditional games into a world of chess pieces, then onward to a museum full of toys and games. Along the way it can become a carved playing piece, a rolling die, or a contraption invented for play.

candidates.name: The Games Board
candidates.why: Historic board and pub games, illustrated game examples, counters, patents and bagatelle tables offer boards, pieces and unusual mechanisms.

candidates.name: Open Chess Museum
candidates.why: Chess sets, carved pieces, boards, mechanical clocks and tournament artifacts give the swarm an array of miniature characters and equipment.

candidates.name: The Strong National Museum of Play
candidates.why: Online exhibits and collections explore board games, puzzles, construction sets, mechanical banks and toys, with plenty of strange forms and ways to play.

candidates.name: Swiss Museum of Games
candidates.why: Exhibitions on games and playing cards introduce illustrated suits, gaming objects and playful inventions from different places and periods.

candidates.name: Deutsches SPIELEmuseum
candidates.why: A museum devoted to historical and modern games, with exhibitions on board games, their components and the many ways people play.

candidates.name: Hudson Museum
candidates.why: Its games and artforms resources include traditional games such as waltes, alongside collections and exhibits full of crafted objects.

candidates.name: Victoria and Albert Museum
candidates.why: The childhood collections include toys, games, dolls and miniature furnishings, while collection stories reveal how playful objects were made and used.

candidates.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
candidates.why: Ancient game boards and pieces include the coiled serpent of Mehen, senet counters and the animal-headed pins of Hounds and Jackals.
